title: A Comprehensive Survey on Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction
domain: Heterogeneous data sources, including unstructured text, semi-structured web pages and tables, images, temporal data, and existing knowledge graphs.
research_problem: The paper addresses the need for a systematic organization of automatic knowledge graph construction methods that can transform heterogeneous, semi-structured, and unstructured data into conceptualized structured knowledge, while also refining and evolving existing graphs in complex big-data environments.
methodology: This is a broad narrative survey rather than a single Text-to-KG system. It defines knowledge graph construction as mapping data sources plus background knowledge into graphs, then organizes reviewed methods in execution and lifecycle order: semi-structured preprocessing; knowledge acquisition through entity discovery, typing, linking, coreference resolution, and relation extraction; knowledge refinement through completion and fusion; knowledge evolution through conditional and temporal knowledge methods; storage; and open research directions. The survey compares methods by data environment, motivation, and architecture.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing and content extraction", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Coreference resolution", "Entity linking and disambiguation", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Knowledge graph completion", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication/entity alignment", "Graph validation and interpretable reasoning", "Graph updating and temporal/conditional evolution"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity linking and disambiguation", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication/entity alignment"]
ontology_schema_use: The survey treats background knowledge as essential to knowledge graph construction. It may be supplied as pre-designed rules, an ontology, a schema, or implicit mathematical principles. The formal KG definition includes concepts, relations, factual triples, and background constraints; YAGO is cited as integrating Wikipedia with a WordNet ontology.

weaknesses: ["Review-level interpretation: the paper is a survey and does not present one reproducible Text-to-KG algorithm or a controlled experimental comparison.", "Review-level interpretation: the very broad scope combines extraction, graph completion, fusion, storage, and evolution, so task-specific results are summarized heterogeneously rather than evaluated under a common benchmark.", "Review-level interpretation: the survey predates the current instruction-tuned and generative LLM methodology family and does not provide a dedicated LLM prompting or fine-tuning taxonomy."]

title: Review of Automatic and Semi-Automatic Creation of Knowledge Graphs from Structured and Unstructured Data
methodology_family: Systematic literature review (not a Text-to-KG methodology family in the supplied taxonomy)
domain: Review corpus of papers about structured/tabular/relational-database data and unstructured natural-language text used for knowledge-graph creation.
research_problem: A systematic review of whether and how knowledge graphs can be created automatically or semi-automatically from structured/tabular or unstructured data, motivated by expert-built domain KGs being time-consuming, error-prone, and unsuitable for large-scale or fast-changing domains.
methodology: The authors searched IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer Link, and ACM Digital Library for 2017–December 2022 using one Boolean query. They deduplicated records; removed books, chapters, surveys, and reviews; screened keywords and abstracts with a second reviewer resolving doubts; then read full papers and reached reviewer consensus. The resulting 19 accessible studies are narratively analyzed by domain, degree of automation, extraction/linking/preprocessing, ontology use, algorithms, storage, and tools.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Ontology or schema discovery", "Graph construction", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication", "Graph storage"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Ontology and schema construction are review topics. The reviewed methods use task-specific ontologies, ontology suites combining taxonomy enrichment and relation discovery, automated class suggestions, Protégé-built ontologies, and the DISK ontology; the review reports that some reviewed papers did not specify an ontology.

domain: Input to this study: scientific articles returned by database searches. Target phenomenon reviewed: unstructured natural-language texts, including web pages, social-media posts, and unstructured textual documents.
research_problem: The paper reviews how unstructured natural-language text can be transformed into RDF subject-predicate-object triples and integrated into an existing ontology-governed knowledge graph; it characterizes methods, benefits, drawbacks, inputs/outputs, automation, applications, and T-Box/A-Box population.
methodology: The authors define six research questions; construct Boolean searches over generation/extraction/construction/population × triples/KG/KB × natural-language/unstructured/textual data; search ACM DL, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, Elsevier Scopus, and ACL Anthology; screen title and abstracts; apply inclusion/exclusion rules; have 15 graduate students review ten articles each with author double-checking; categorize papers, generate metadata, filter the 150 retrieved records to 15 closely aligned papers, then report quantitative, qualitative, and category-based synthesis. The review categories are language specificity, transformer use, T-Box/A-Box population, lexical resources, domain specificity, and link creation.

title: Constructing Knowledge Graphs from Text Using Large Language Models: Scoping Review
domain: Unstructured textual data, including raw documents, corpora, short texts, and domain documents such as healthcare, policy, education, legal, manufacturing, and general-knowledge text.
research_problem: The paper addresses the lack of methodological standardization and consolidated evidence about techniques that use LLMs to construct knowledge graphs from unstructured text. Its objective is to map existing approaches, compare their effectiveness and characteristics, and identify benefits, limitations, and research gaps.
methodology: This is a PRISMA-based scoping review, not a single Text-to-KG system. The review has planning, execution, and reporting phases. It searches Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and ACM using the query “Knowledge Graph” AND (“Large Language Model” OR “LLM” OR “Generative Pre-trained Transformers”) AND text; screens studies using eligibility criteria; extracts bibliographic and methodological information; and synthesizes 126 included primary studies into four categories. The reviewed execution patterns are: RDF-based ontology selection, LLM-assisted extraction and RDF serialization; prompt-based direct structured-triple extraction; RAG-based retrieval followed by enriched LLM triple generation and graph integration; and hybrid NLP extraction followed by LLM refinement, validation, or augmentation and graph storage.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Coreference resolution", "Relation and triple extraction", "Ontology or schema discovery and selection", "Graph construction and RDF serialization", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication", "Graph validation and correction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction"]
ontology_schema_use: Ontology/schema use varies by reviewed category. RDF-Based methods explicitly define a domain and select existing ontologies, provide ontology text, links, or descriptions to the LLM, align extracted elements with established vocabularies, serialize RDF, and store triples. Prompt-Based methods generally do not rely on predefined ontologies. RAG-Based methods use external document bases, wikis, databases, or existing graphs as retrieved context but usually do not enforce formal schema alignment. Hybrid Pipelines may align final triples with ontologies depending on their NLP configuration.
datasets: ["Scoping-review corpus of 126 included primary studies", "Search-result pool: 321 retrieved studies from Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and ACM on 31 March 2025"]
evaluation_metrics: ["Recall", "Recall variants", "F1-score", "Precision", "SimKGC", "WN18RR"]
main_results: ["The review analyzed 126 primary studies and grouped them into four categories: RDF-Based (50 studies), Prompt-Based (35), RAG-Based (22), and Hybrid Pipelines (19).", "Among 36 studies that compared multiple models, OpenAI GPT was most frequently used, followed by LLAMA and ChatGLM; GPT-4 and its branches were the most common GPT versions.", "When application domains were specified, general knowledge was most frequent, followed by health and manufacturing processes.", "The review identifies automation, scalability, and precision as recurring advantages, and manual curation, limited generalization, and low precision as recurring limitations.", "RDF-Based methods emphasize formal ontologies, RDF serialization, semantic interoperability, and SPARQL querying; Prompt-Based methods emphasize direct triple extraction without supervised fine-tuning or predefined ontologies; RAG-Based methods add retrieved external context; Hybrid Pipelines combine classical NLP extraction with LLM refinement, validation, or augmentation.", "The review reports that no single approach resolves all challenges and that prompt- and RAG-based methods are more flexible but less reproducible, while RDF-based and hybrid methods provide greater structural control and interpretability."]
strengths: ["The review uses an explicit PRISMA-adapted protocol with stated research questions, databases, search string, eligibility criteria, extraction stages, and synthesis procedure.", "It provides a compact taxonomy of four recurring LLM-based KG-construction patterns and further subdivides prompt-based methods into zero-shot prompting, sequential prompt chaining, and template-driven prompting.", "It compares approaches along useful dimensions: ontology alignment, prompting role, supervision, reproducibility, semantic control, scalability, and interpretability.", "It identifies recurring cross-study benefits and limitations rather than presenting only isolated paper summaries."]

author_limitations: ["The rapidly evolving field may have caused very recent research not yet indexed in the consulted sources to be excluded.", "Persistent challenges across the reviewed studies include low precision, the need for manual curation, and limited generalization across domains.", "Methodological heterogeneity, variable evaluation metrics, and the absence of standardized benchmarks complicate direct comparisons.", "The paper notes that LLM-generated outputs may hallucinate, have poor support for complex relations, fail to resolve contradictions or conflicting RDF knowledge, and require expert validation in some hybrid settings."]
review_inferences: ["Develop standardized metrics for evaluating LLM-generated knowledge graphs.", "Explore models and methods that mitigate hallucinations and improve extraction reliability, accuracy, and computational efficiency.", "Review-level inference: future syntheses should enforce explicit overlap accounting, harmonize category definitions with Text-to-KG stages, and report compatible dataset/task/split/metric associations before comparing methods."]
unresolved_problems: ["Low precision, false positives, semantic ambiguity, and systemic errors in named-entity recognition and triple generation remain unresolved.", "Manual curation and expert validation are still required for system configuration, ontology development, rule-based setups, and high-precision output.", "Generalization across domains remains limited, especially where methods depend on rigid models or domain-specific resources.", "Hallucinations, inability to resolve contradictions or conflicting knowledge, and weak handling of complex relations remain open problems.", "The field lacks standardized benchmarks and consistent evaluation metrics, making cross-method comparison difficult.", "Prompt and RAG methods remain sensitive to nondeterminism and may lack formal grounding, symbolic reasoning, automated validation, or ontology integration."]

title: OpenIE-based Approach for Knowledge Graph construction from text
domain: English plain text extracted from IT-news webpages (with webpage HTML cleaned before processing).
research_problem: Transform unstructured English text into a Knowledge Graph/RDF representation while addressing sparse or inconsistent entity linking, choosing subject/object entities in OpenIE relations, linking relation phrases to identifiers, and representing relation context that a single RDF triple would omit.
methodology: Execution-order pipeline: (1) acquire IT-news webpages and clean them to plain text; (2) Stanford CoreNLP performs sentence segmentation, POS tagging, constituency parsing, and filters sentences to 5–25 words with an NP–verb–NP pattern; (3) invoke DBpedia Spotlight, Babelfy, and TagMe for entity mentions and DBpedia-linked IRIs, then resolve overlaps by maximal match, choose conflicting links by majority vote, and deduplicate; (4) associate selected entities with constituency-tree noun phrases by surface-form matching; (5) extract binary relations using ClausIE; (6) run Mate-Tools SRL to match the OpenIE predicate to PropBank senses and identify Agent/A0 and Patient/A1; (7) when SRL is partial or absent, use rule-based nearest-entity and subject/object fallbacks; (8) query Premon by predicate sense to obtain an IRI; (9) create event-centred n-ary RDF/TriG named graphs with agent, patient, NP memberships, sentence provenance, and relation comment; optionally store them in a graph store.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Uses Semantic Web RDF and named graphs; DBpedia supplies entity IRIs; PropBank predicate senses are mapped to Premon IRIs through SPARQL; Gold vocabulary represents agent/patient roles, dcterms:isPartOf represents entity membership in noun-phrase resources, and NIF preserves sentence context. It does not map predicates to a domain ontology property; it models them as event types in an n-ary representation.

baselines: ["EEL: Babelfy, DBpedia Spotlight, and TagMe individual systems.", "OpenIE relation extraction: Stanford OIE and OIE4, compared with ClausIE.", "RDF coherence: ablated version of the authors' system without noun-phrase/entity association."]
evaluation_metrics: ["Precision", "Recall", "F1 (harmonic mean with beta=1)", "Free-marginal multi-rater Kappa", "Overall inter-rater agreement", "RDF counts: entities, extracted relations, RDF-represented relations/events, RDF statements"]
main_results: ["On 100 IT-news sentences, the EEL integration obtained P=0.8139, R=0.9643, F1=0.8827 and 731 entities; TagMe obtained F1=0.8305, Spotlight F1=0.6566, and Babelfy F1=0.6242. Spotlight had the highest precision (0.8560) but lowest recall (0.5325).", "On 100 IT-news sentences, ClausIE obtained P=0.638, R=0.620, F1=0.628 for relation extraction, versus OIE4 F1=0.580 and Stanford OIE F1=0.330.", "Across 12,015 sentences, the pipeline produced 103,401 linked entities, 41,190 extracted relations, 12,686 RDF-represented events/relations, and 89,486 RDF statements.", "For 50 manually judged RDF events, median precision was 0.72 for subject/agent, 0.89 predicate, 0.64 object/patient, 0.82 semantic relation, and 0.51 complete triple. The NP-association ablation changed these to 0.50, 0.90, 0.46, 0.80, and 0.26, respectively.", "Inter-rater Kappa was 0.4533 subject, 0.6466 predicate, 0.3133 object, 0.7000 relation, and 0.3800 triple."]
strengths: ["Author-reported: combining EEL systems improves F1 relative to each individual evaluated EEL tool (0.8827 versus the best individual 0.8305).", "Author-reported: noun-phrase/entity association improves judged RDF subject, object, relation, and complete-triple precision over the no-NP-association ablation.", "Review-level inference: the event-centred n-ary representation retains multiple linked entities, semantic roles, original sentence context, and relation text, making provenance and contextual qualifiers more explicit than a bare binary triple.", "Review-level inference: the modular pipeline permits replacement of the chosen OpenIE, EEL, SRL, or storage tool without changing the stated RDF-preparation logic."]

title: Semi-Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction by Relation Pattern Extraction
domain: Enterprise-company webpages containing semi-structured textual fields and DOM structure
research_problem: The paper addresses semi-automatic extraction of relation-object facts from enterprise web pages when the same relation has different textual representations, website templates vary across sources, and templates change over time. It aims to reduce the manual annotation burden while constructing a knowledge graph and discovering previously unseen relations.
methodology: The system parses webpages into DOM trees and represents each relation-object instance as two XPath-derived tag sequences containing the relation and object text. Tag tokens are embedded with a Skip-Gram word2vec model trained on DOM-parsing output. Concatenated embeddings are processed by two shared five-layer fully connected feature-map networks forming a Siamese architecture. The learned distance metric identifies similar instances, whose centroid forms a relation pattern. Seed patterns are iteratively expanded and refined with newly extracted instances; clustering of instances is additionally used to detect patterns for new relations.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Ontology or schema discovery"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction"]
ontology_schema_use: No external ontology is reported. Existing relation names and manually supplied seed relation instances define the initial relation schema; newly discovered relation clusters are not automatically assigned semantic labels.
datasets: ["Enterprise Knowledge Graph dataset: Japanese company websites; 2,717,653 company entities and 22,257,276 triples", "Ten-relation similarity-learning subset with 286,276 instances: name, address, person, homepage, phone number, rel-org, finance, size, date, and product", "Unseen relation dataset: fax, email, permission, introduction, domains, and offices"]
evaluation_metrics: ["False Accept Rate (FA)", "False Reject Rate (FR)", "Equal Error Rate (EER)", "Precision", "Recall"]
main_results: ["On the ten known relations, using 10,000 instances and 100 iteration steps produced EER 0.04; using 10,000 instances and 500 iteration steps produced EER 0.01.", "On the unseen-relation dataset, the system achieved EER 0.05.", "For clustering-based new-relation detection, K-Means generally outperformed hierarchical clustering in the reported precision/recall results. title: From Text to Knowledge: Bridging the Gap with Probabilistic Graphical Models
domain: Unstructured natural-language text: general free-text sentences, PubMed/MEDLINE abstracts, and GeneRIF biomedical phrases. The broader thesis also uses documents with existing semantic annotations for topic-model-based discovery.
research_problem: The thesis addresses the gap between facts buried in unstructured textual collections and queryable structured knowledge. Its direct Text-to-KG problem is: given typed entities and relations, extract entity mentions and typed relations from text, normalize them to URIs, and arrange the resulting facts as an entity-relationship graph. The principal applied case is extraction of typed human gene-disease associations from biomedical text.
methodology: Text2SemRel is a supervised, schema-guided extraction pipeline. First, a document collection is annotated using entity classes and relation types from a conceptual schema. A linear-chain CRF learns NER and semantic-relation-extraction (SRE) labels using lexical, orthographic, word-shape, character n-gram, contextual-window, and dictionary features. The one-step CRF jointly labels entities and relations for encyclopaedic-style text with a known key entity. The cascaded CRF first predicts entities with an NER CRF, passes role features to an SRE CRF, and is used for general free text; when more than two entity mentions are predicted, it examines N-best Viterbi label sequences. Candidate facts are checked against relation domain/range constraints, entity mentions are normalized by strict controlled-vocabulary matching plus a sliding-window expansion/shrinking heuristic, and valid triples are stored. The thesis additionally develops unsupervised Topic-Concept and User-Topic-Concept extensions of LDA for discovery over already semantically annotated document collections; these models are not the Text2SemRel KG-construction component.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Graph validation and correction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: A supplied conceptual schema/semantic data model defines entity classes, binary relation labels, and each relation's domain and range. It constrains fact acceptance so that only schema-consistent pairs are stored. Controlled vocabularies/thesauri provide entity URIs for canonicalization; in the biomedical implementation, disease names and synonyms come from the MeSH C branch and existing Bio2RDF namespaces supply identifiers. The extracted facts can populate a formal ontology and are serialized as RDF/N-triples.

title: Joint Extraction of Entities and Relations Based on a Novel Graph Scheme
domain: Unstructured natural-language text sentences
research_problem: The paper addresses joint extraction of entity mentions and semantic relations from unstructured sentences. It targets the limitation of prior neural methods that separately extract entities and relations and obtain joint learning mainly through parameter sharing, without fully exploiting dependencies between output entities, relations, and relation labels. It also addresses the inability of a prior tagging scheme to identify overlapping relations.
methodology: The method represents each sentence as a directed graph whose nodes correspond to input words. Entity arcs encode internal entity structure, while labeled relation arcs connect entity nodes. A transition system incrementally performs entity-generation and relation-generation actions over stacks, a buffer, partial entity chunks, relation arcs, and entity arcs. A Bi-LSTM encodes token context; stack LSTMs represent parser state; recursive composition functions update entity representations when relation arcs are created. A neural classifier assigns valid transition actions, and greedy decoding generates the final graph. Preconditions permit nodes to have multiple heads, supporting overlapping relations.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing"]
ontology_schema_use: The system uses a predefined set of relation labels and entity labels/types supplied by the task/dataset. It does not discover an ontology or schema; the graph scheme defines the representation of entity arcs and labeled relation arcs.

title: Seq2KG: An End-to-End Neural Model for Domain Agnostic Knowledge Graph Construction from Text
methodology_family: End-to-end neural sequence labelling model (Seq2KG) that jointly performs triple extraction and entity typing as a multi-label sequence labelling task
domain: Unstructured natural language text (news articles/documents and single sentences)
research_problem: Traditional KGC from text relies on entity/relation linking to an existing knowledge base, but many domains lack a knowledge base, and important information held in phrases that are not standard named entities is lost, so there is a need for a domain-agnostic method that constructs true knowledge graphs (with node attributes) from text without assuming availability of an external knowledge base.
methodology: Seq2KG embeds an input sequence with BERT, passes it through one or more Bi-GRU layers, and jointly predicts (a) multi-label triple-membership tags for each token, indicating its role as head/relation/tail of zero or more triples, and (b) entity-type labels for head/tail tokens, using a joint categorical cross-entropy loss averaged across the two components; triples are reconstructed from contiguous spans sharing the same triple-membership label.
pipeline_stages: ["Triple mapping", "Triple filtering", "BERT embedding", "Bi-GRU sequence labelling for triple membership", "Entity typing of head/tail nodes"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity typing of head/tail nodes"]
relation_extraction: ["Triple mapping", "Triple filtering", "Bi-GRU sequence labelling for triple membership"]
datasets: ["Catering Services (CS)", "Automotive Engineering (AE)", "BBN"]
baselines: ["Rule-based model", "Filtering model"]
evaluation_metrics: ["Strict Accuracy", "Loose Macro", "Loose Micro", "Strict acc"]

title: An Autoregressive Text-to-Graph Framework for Joint Entity and Relation Extraction
domain: Unstructured English natural-language text tokenized as an input sequence; experimental inputs include newswire/news-related text, AI-paper abstracts, and ACE 05 multi-domain text.
research_problem: Jointly extract typed entity mentions and typed relations from unstructured text as an information-extraction graph, avoiding the error propagation of sequential entity-recognition and relation-classification pipelines and improving source-text grounding in generative extraction.
methodology: ATG first encodes the input tokens with a transformer and enumerates bounded candidate spans. It computes each typed-span embedding from the encoder representations of the span boundaries, then forms a dynamic decoder vocabulary from these span embeddings plus learned relation-type and special-token embeddings. A causal transformer decoder autoregressively emits typed entity-span nodes, <SEP>, then head-span, tail-span, relation-type edge triplets, ending with <END>. Decoder inputs combine token, positional, and structural-role embeddings. Training maximizes the likelihood of a sorted or random graph linearization, with sentence-concatenation augmentation to reduce premature termination. At inference, a state-transition constrained decoder only permits valid graph sequences, prevents duplicate entities, prevents self-relations, and can restrict relations by entity-type/domain constraints.
pipeline_stages: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing"]
ontology_schema_use: The method uses a closed, dataset-provided schema of entity types and relation types: typed spans and relation types are decoder-vocabulary items. During constrained decoding, compatible relations may additionally be restricted using domain knowledge, illustrated by PER-to-ORG allowing Work_For on CoNLL 04. It does not discover an ontology or schema.

title: LlmRe: A Zero-Shot Entity Relation Extraction Method Based on the Large Language Model
domain: Unstructured or semi-structured natural-language text, including examples such as news, microblogs, and literature; the experiments use Chinese text samples.
research_problem: The paper addresses entity-relation extraction from unstructured or semi-structured text when task-specific labeled data are unavailable. It aims to reduce the cost and domain-specificity of conventional supervised extraction, control large-language-model output randomness, and produce structured knowledge triples usable for knowledge-graph construction.
methodology: LlmRe is a sequential, prompt-based extraction pipeline. The user supplies an extraction schema mapping relation types to head and tail entity types. First, ChatGLM is prompted with the sentence and a head-entity type to extract candidate heads. Second, the schema determines compatible tail types, and ChatGLM extracts candidate tails for each type. Regular expressions parse the model responses into typed dictionaries. Third, candidate heads and tails are combined with schema-compatible relations; ChatGLM is prompted with the original sentence and each candidate triple, and returns a Boolean-style YES/NO judgment. Accepted triples are emitted. In-context demonstrations constrain the output format, while the model parameters remain unchanged.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction: extract head and tail entities from text.", "Entity typing: extract entities according to schema-defined entity types."]
relation_extraction: ["Relation and triple extraction: assemble compatible candidates and verify relations with the LLM.", "Graph construction: not performed in the paper; accepted triples are presented as usable output for knowledge-graph construction."]
ontology_schema_use: A user-provided extraction schema is required. It is a dictionary whose keys are relation types and whose values specify the head entity type and tail entity type. The schema constrains candidate tail types, compatible relations, candidate-triple assembly, and relation verification; no external ontology or knowledge base is reported.

title: Fine-Tuning Language Models for Triple Extraction with Data Augmentation

research_problem: Extract subject–predicate–object triples directly from unstructured/plain-text sentences so that text-derived facts can populate knowledge graphs, while improving contextual relation extraction and adherence to the DBpedia ontology format.
methodology: The authors construct augmented WebNLG training variants in execution order: Text2triples examples; GPT-3.5-generated extraction explanations; Triples2text reconstruction examples; and reflection examples that validate or correct generated triples. They then apply PEFT/LoRA supervised fine-tuning with HuggingFace tooling, merge LoRA weights with each base model, run prompted inference on test sentences, and compare generated triples with reference triples under four matching criteria.

title: CodeKGC: Code Language Model for Generative Knowledge Graph Construction
methodology_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
domain: Unstructured natural-language sentences, transformed into Python-like code prompts with natural-language docstrings, schema class definitions, and optionally in-context demonstration/rationale code.
research_problem: Generative knowledge graph construction from unstructured natural-language text, specifically extraction of relational triples while reducing the difficulty that flattened serializations have with structural dependencies, overlapping facts, and long-range relations.
methodology: Execution pipeline: (1) use a predefined Python-conformant script to convert input text T and gold/output triple graph G into code-format Tc and Gc; (2) construct a schema-aware prompt with Entity, Relation, Triple, and Extract classes, where entity/relation types inherit from base classes; (3) append k in-context completed examples, optionally including rationales; (4) generate a rationale that first identifies candidate relations and then corresponding entities; (5) generate Extract([Triple(...)]) code; and (6) convert generated code back to triples/graph G. The main large-model runs use text-davinci-002 or text-davinci-003, with code-davinci-002 in ablations.
pipeline_stages: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing"]
ontology_schema_use: Uses a predefined KG schema as prompt-time structural guidance, rather than discovering an ontology. Python base classes Entity and Relation encode entity/relation definitions; typed subclasses and Triple instances represent permitted graph structure, including entity-type constraints.
datasets: ["ADE: adverse-drug-event texts; 1 adverse-effect relation and 2 entity types (disease, drug); 300 randomly selected test samples evaluated because of API-time constraints", "CoNLL04: 4 relations and 3 entity types", "SciERC: scientific-paper information extraction; 7 relations and 6 entity types", "T-REx: 838,821 sentences, 4,378,318 triples, 10,496 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)", "TEKGEN: 6,310,061 sentences, 10,609,697 triples, 1,013 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)", "KELM: 15,616,551 sentences, 35,117,608 triples, 59,904 relations (smaller-model code pre-training)"]
baselines: ["UIE (supervised comparable SOTA)", "Vanilla Prompt with text-davinci-002", "Vanilla Prompt with text-davinci-003", "Prompt variations without schema-aware prompt", "Prompt variations without rationale", "Smaller-model comparisons: pre-trained/not-pre-trained T5 and CodeT5"]
evaluation_metrics: ["Relation strict micro F1; a predicted triple is correct only when head entity, tail entity, and relation all exactly match. Entity types are predicted but excluded from F1."]
main_results: ["Table 2 zero-shot relation-strict micro F1: CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 scores 43.7 on ADE, 41.6 on CoNLL04, and 19.5 on SciERC; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 scores 42.5, 35.8, and 15.0, respectively.", "Table 2 few-shot relation-strict micro F1: CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 scores 64.2 on ADE, 49.6 on CoNLL04, and 24.7 on SciERC; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 scores 61.5, 42.7, and 18.5.", "In few-shot mode, CodeKGC/text-davinci-003 exceeds its matched Vanilla Prompt by 5.4 F1 on ADE, 6.4 on CoNLL04, and 5.9 on SciERC. It also exceeds UIE on all three few-shot results in Table 2.", "On CoNLL04 prompt-variation experiments, Figure 5 reports that both schema-aware prompting and rationale-enhanced generation improve CodeKGC relative to their ablations; the paper warns that lengthy rationale prompts can hurt when sample size is too small.", "For the smaller-model ADE study, Figure 8 shows restructured-code-pretrained T5 at 75.6 and CodeT5 at 68.6 F1, below UIE at 81.1; non-pretrained models score 58.8 (T5) and 52.2 (CodeT5)."]
strengths: ["Author claim: schema-aware Python-format prompts explicitly represent entity, relation, property, and constraint structure through class definitions and typed triple instances.", "Experimental result: the large-model CodeKGC prompt consistently exceeds its matched Vanilla Prompt in the Table 2 few-shot setting and improves zero-shot results on every reported dataset/backbone pair.", "Experimental result: code formatting helps on long-range and overlapping-triple cases when paired with a strong code model; Figure 7 provides qualitative examples.", "Review-level inference: representing schema and triples in an executable-style, typed code syntax makes the generated output easier to parse deterministically than unconstrained free-form text, provided the generated code follows the prescribed template."]
weaknesses: ["Author-reported experimental finding: ADE performance is limited because the medical corpus contains many acronyms; in zero-shot mode CodeKGC is similar to Vanilla Prompt.", "Author-reported limitation: performance on complex structures depends heavily on a powerful code-pretrained backbone; CodeKGC/text-davinci-002 can underperform Vanilla Prompt/text-davinci-002 on sampled hard examples.", "Experimental result: the 770M restructured-code-pretrained models remain below UIE on ADE (best 75.6 versus UIE 81.1).", "Review-level inference: the approach requires predefined entity and relation schemas and hand-designed code prompts, so transfer to a new schema needs schema encoding and prompt/example preparation rather than being fully schema-free."]
author_limitations: ["Rationale-enhanced prompts can negatively affect performance when the sample size is too small because prompts become lengthy.", "For complex structural examples, CodeKGC heavily relies on a more powerful code-pretrained model.", "Limited parameter space creates a trade-off between semantic understanding and code generation in smaller models.", "The paper identifies its present code prompts as needing refinement to capture entity/relation nuances better."]

title: iText2KG: Incremental Knowledge Graphs Construction Using Large Language Models
methodology_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
domain: Raw unstructured natural-language documents: website text, scientific articles, and CVs; documents are rewritten into JSON semantic blocks before entity and relation extraction.
research_problem: Construct consistent knowledge graphs incrementally from raw, unstructured documents while reducing semantically duplicated or unresolved entities and relations. The objective is a topic- and document-type-independent, zero-shot alternative to ontology-dependent and supervised KG-construction pipelines.
methodology: Execution order: (1) Document Distiller prompts an LLM with each raw document/chunk and a user-defined JSON-like blueprint, producing and aggregating semi-filled JSON semantic blocks. (2) iEntities Matcher extracts entities from the first block, then for each later block extracts local entities and incrementally matches them to global entities by exact membership or cosine-similarity threshold, updating the global entity set. (3) iRelations Matcher receives each semantic block and either global or locally matched entities as context; it extracts relations and incrementally resolves them analogously. Global context permits direct and implied relations but can add irrelevant edges; local context targets direct relations. (4) global entities and relations are loaded into Neo4j for graph construction and visualization.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication", "Graph validation and correction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: The method accepts a user-defined schema/blueprint, implemented as a predefined JSON structure parsed with LangChain, to guide which textual values are distilled. The authors explicitly distinguish this flexible blueprint from an ontology; it biases extraction toward classes/keys but is intended to remain adaptable across use cases.

baselines: ["Graph Construction using OpenAI Function Method", "LangChain graph construction", "LlamaIndex property-graph construction (not evaluated in entity/relation-resolution FDR tables because authors state it produces unconnected RAG-oriented subgraphs)"]
evaluation_metrics: ["Schema Consistency score", "Information Consistency categories: very different (<30%), medium (30–60%), largely consistent (60–90%), fully consistent (>90%)", "Triplet Extraction Precision", "Entity/Relation Resolution False Discovery Rate", "Mean and standard deviation of cosine similarity for entity and relationship matching data"]
main_results: ["Experimental result: Document Distiller schema consistency was 0.97 ± 0.09 for CVs, 0.98 ± 0.04 for scientific articles, and 0.94 ± 0.13 for websites.", "Experimental result: fully/largely consistent distilled content was 74.5%/25.5% for CVs, 57.1%/42.9% for scientific articles, and 56.0%/24.0% for websites; websites also had 20.0% medium consistency.", "Experimental result: local entity context produced higher relevant-triplet precision than global context: Computer Science 0.94 ± 0.06 versus 0.83 ± 0.06; Music 0.90 ± 0.07 versus 0.81 ± 0.05.", "Experimental result: iText2KG entity FDR was 0.01 ± 0.01 for scientific articles, 0 for CVs, and 0 for websites; relation FDR was 0.01 ± 0.01, 0, and 0, respectively. OpenAI Function/LangChain had entity FDR 0.11/0.14 (articles) and 0.31/0.29 (websites), and relation FDR 0.07/0.06 and 0.15/0.14, respectively."]
strengths: ["Author claim: flexible user-defined blueprints make the method adaptable to structured and unstructured document types without a universal ontology.", "Experimental result: incremental entity/relation resolution achieved lower reported FDR than the evaluated OpenAI Function and LangChain baselines for scientific-article and website scenarios.", "Experimental result: separating entity extraction from relation extraction supports two operating points: local context for higher precision and global context for richer, implied-relation extraction.", "Review-level inference: the explicit intermediate semantic-block and global-entity representations make the source of graph nodes and edges more inspectable than a single direct text-to-graph generation step."]
weaknesses: ["Author-reported trade-off: global entity context enriches the graph with implied relations but lowers triplet precision by about 10 percentage points and increases the chance of irrelevant relations.", "Author-reported dependency: output focus is controlled by a user-supplied blueprint whose design varies by application; there is no universal blueprint.", "Review-level inference: the evaluation is limited in scale for distillation (five items of each document type), and triplet ground truth includes manual checking after the authors found the referenced dataset non-exhaustive; this limits certainty about generalization and reproducibility of those measurements.", "Review-level inference: the paper reports extraction precision and unresolved-duplicate FDR, but does not report recall, end-to-end graph completeness, cost, latency, or inter-annotator agreement for manual checks."]
author_limitations: ["The cosine-similarity matching threshold is a hyperparameter: an upper threshold such as 0.7 is selected for high precision, while a lower threshold reduces resolution specificity.", "Global-context relation extraction has a precision-versus-richness trade-off because it can generate irrelevant implied relations.", "Websites are more difficult than CVs and scientific articles because their content is more unstructured; larger numbers of chunks also increase noisy nodes and make resolution important."]
review_inferences: ["Author-proposed improvement: enhance cosine-similarity metrics for entity and relation matching.", "Author-proposed improvement: eliminate manual definition of the matching threshold hyperparameter.", "Author-proposed improvement: integrate entity type as a parameter in matching.", "Review-level inference: evaluate the global-versus-local context choice with a precision-and-recall/completeness protocol so that implied-relation gains are measured rather than described only as graph enrichment."]
unresolved_problems: ["Author-stated unresolved problem: robustly matching semantically similar entities and relations without a manually selected cosine-similarity threshold remains open.", "Author-stated unresolved problem: choosing between globally contextualized, richer but less precise relations and locally contextualized, more precise but less enriched relations remains application-dependent.", "Review-level inference: reliable evaluation of implied triples and whole-graph completeness remains unresolved in this study because the authors augment a non-exhaustive annotated dataset with manual checks and report precision rather than recall."]
reproducibility: The paper states that code and dataset are available at https://github.com/AuvaLab/itext2kg. It also states that the threshold-estimation entity-pair and relationship datasets are available in that repository.

title: Leveraging LLM for Automated Ontology Extraction and Knowledge Graph Generation
methodology_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific model training)
domain: User-provided predefined ontology or targeted natural-language text for ontology extraction, followed by comprehensive unstructured engineering-domain text; the source document may contain text, tables, and graphs, but the case study primarily uses textual content.
research_problem: Automate extraction and organization of relevant, structured knowledge from long, complex Reliability and Maintainability technical documents, especially semiconductor-equipment material, because manual extraction and KG construction are labor-intensive, error-prone, and may yield incomplete or inconsistent representations. The objective is a user-tailored ontology and KG that supports querying, analysis, and decision-making.
methodology: OntoKGen is an interactive, human-in-the-loop LLM system using OpenAI's API and an adaptive iterative CoT algorithm. Execution order: (1) the user supplies a predefined ontology or targeted text; (2) the LLM proposes/refines concepts, then relationships, then node properties, each confirmed by the user; (3) the confirmed ontology becomes the schema blueprint; (4) comprehensive text is supplied; (5) creation iterates over ontology concepts to create nodes and properties, then over relationships to create edges, then fills properties; (6) review re-reads the text for missing aligned instances/relations and reviews the graph for incorrect, unconnected, or missing links; (7) on approval, the system generates Cypher MERGE commands to populate Neo4j. Conversation history is retained to maintain context and guide users back to the active stage.

In the case study it included Equipment System, Equipment States, Sub-States, Activities, and Metrics; Has State, Has Sub-State, Has Activity, and Has Metric; mandatory id and name plus a user-specified brief explanation. The system uses the ontology as a structural blueprint to avoid ambiguity and enforce a consistent graph.

title: Prompt Me One More Time: A Two-Step Knowledge Extraction Pipeline with Ontology-Based Verification
domain: Unstructured natural-language text, including SynthIE synthetic texts and manually sampled Wikipedia paragraphs.
research_problem: How to extend Wikidata from unstructured text with accurate, canonical Wikidata triples without training a separate extractor for each evolving KG or ontology. The work targets error-prone entity/relation normalization and LLM hallucinations after extraction.
methodology: Execution pipeline: (1) prompt gpt-3.5-turbo to emit JSON subject–relation–object candidate triples from text, using in-context examples; (2) use a FAISS dense-retrieval index built from pretrained Contriever embeddings to retrieve the top five similar canonical Wikidata names for every candidate subject, relation, and object; (3) prompt the LLM again to choose context-appropriate canonical names only from each retrieved list and output refined JSON triples; (4) query Wikidata type hierarchies and apply the extracted relation's subject and value constraints, retaining a triple only when subject and object hierarchy types align with those constraints.
pipeline_stages: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Graph validation and correction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Wikidata supplies the target KG ontology, canonical entity and relation names, subject/value property constraints, and P31 ('instance of') and P279 ('subclass of') type hierarchies. Verification is post-processing: it filters triples inconsistent with relation constraints; the ontology is not supplied in the refinement prompt because that would make it unreasonably large.
datasets: ["SynthIE-text-small", "Wiki-cIE Code training split (source of in-context examples)", "WikicIE-test-small (100 random samples used to select matched Wikipedia paragraphs)", "Natural Language corpora: 100 manually sampled Wikipedia paragraphs"]
baselines: ["SynthIE T5-large, reported as the best-reported model trained on SynthIE and fine-tuned on SynthIE-text-small"]
evaluation_metrics: ["F1", "Precision", "Recall", "Mean and standard deviation over three runs with different in-context examples", "Human-evaluated precision", "Number of correct triples", "Intersection over union (IoU) of correct triples between models"]
main_results: ["On SynthIE-text-small, the full pipeline achieved F1 0.55±0.01, precision 0.59±0.03, and recall 0.52±0.005.", "Removing verification gave F1 0.53±0.01, precision 0.55±0.03, recall 0.52±0.005; removing refinement gave F1 0.51±0.01, precision 0.60±0.03, recall 0.44±0.006. Without in-context examples, F1 was 0.16, precision 0.65, recall 0.09.", "On SynthIE-text-small, fine-tuned SynthIE T5-large scored F1 0.88, precision 0.87, recall 0.88, versus the proposed pipeline's 0.55/0.59/0.52.", "On the human-evaluated natural-language corpus, the proposed method had precision 0.74 with 187 correct triples, versus 0.55 and 201 for SynthIE T5-large; correct-triple IoU was 0.08."]
strengths: ["The pipeline requires no task-specific fine-tuning and can normalize open-text extractions to canonical Wikidata names through retrieval plus a second prompt.", "Refinement materially improves recall in the reported ablation (0.44 without refinement to 0.52 full pipeline), while ontology filtering improves precision after refinement (0.55 without verification to 0.59 full pipeline).", "The method has higher human-evaluated precision than the fine-tuned SynthIE baseline on the paper's matched natural-language Wikipedia set (0.74 versus 0.55)."]

title: KnowledgeNet: A Benchmark Dataset for Knowledge Base Population

research_problem: The paper addresses the lack of a benchmark dataset supporting holistic end-to-end evaluation of Knowledge Base Population (KBP) systems, since prior datasets/evaluations (e.g., TAC) are non-exhaustive, hard to reproduce, or suited only for evaluating individual subcomponents (entity linking, relation extraction) rather than the full KBP pipeline, and traditional pipeline systems suffer from error propagation.
methodology: KnowledgeNet is built via a four-step annotation framework (fetch sentences, detect mentions, classify facts, link entities) that produces (subject; property; object) triples linked to the Wikidata knowledge base (KB). title: Text2KGBench: A Benchmark for Ontology-Driven Knowledge Graph Generation from Text
domain: A natural-language sentence, its associated ontology verbalization (concepts and relation signatures), a fixed extraction instruction, and one or more sentence-to-triple demonstrations from training data.
research_problem: The paper addresses the lack of an evaluation benchmark for extracting sentence-grounded KG facts with an explicit ontology as input. It evaluates whether language models can select canonical ontology relations, extract facts faithful to a sentence rather than model pretraining knowledge, and avoid fabricated subjects, relations, or objects.
methodology: Text2KGBench specifies ontology-guided sentence-level fact extraction. For each case, a prompt combines: (1) a fixed instruction to output only triples, (2) a verbalized ontology listing concepts and canonical relations with domain/range signatures, (3) a similarity-selected training demonstration with its aligned triples, and (4) the test sentence. The decoder-only instruction-tuned LLM directly generates triples in relation(subject, object) notation. The benchmark parses these as output triples and evaluates exact fact extraction, use of ontology relations, and hallucinated subject/relation/object terms. The authors' baseline retrieves demonstrations using SBERT with T5-XXL sentence embeddings.
pipeline_stages: ["Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Graph validation and correction"]
ontology_schema_use: Ontology is a required task input and prompt context. It specifies concepts, canonical relation names, and relation domain/range constraints. The current conformance metric checks whether the output relation name is in the ontology; the paper notes that validation could later extend to domain/range and other axioms. Ontologies are verbalized rather than supplied as direct RDF/OWL syntax.

title: KGGen: Extracting Knowledge Graphs from Plain Text with Language Models
domain: Unstructured plain-text documents or text chunks
research_problem: The paper addresses the scarcity and incompleteness of useful knowledge graphs generated from unstructured text. Existing OpenIE and GraphRAG extraction methods are described as producing sparse, disconnected graphs because they lack effective entity resolution and relation normalization, which limits downstream retrieval and graph-embedding utility. KGGen aims to extract dense, information-preserving graphs with more reusable entities and relation types.
methodology: KGGen first prompts Gemini 2.0 Flash to extract entities from each text unit, then prompts it to extract subject-predicate-object triples whose subjects and objects must come from the entity list. It aggregates graphs across source texts using lowercase normalization and then resolves duplicate entities and edges. Resolution embeds items with S-BERT, clusters them with k-means into groups of 128, retrieves 16 semantically similar candidates using fused BM25 and embedding similarity, and asks an LLM to identify duplicates and select canonical aliases. The process repeats until each cluster is resolved.

ontology_schema_use: No domain ontology is used. KGGen imposes a lightweight schema through prompted structured output: entities are subjects or objects and relations are subject-predicate-object triples. The relation-resolution prompt constrains duplicate decisions to equivalent meanings and selects a canonical alias.

title: Knowledge Vault: A Web-Scale Approach to Probabilistic Knowledge Fusion
domain: Web-scale unstructured and semi-structured Web content: free text documents, HTML DOM trees, HTML tables, and human-authored schema.org annotations; existing Freebase triples are also input as graph priors and distant-supervision seeds.
research_problem: Constructing a much larger knowledge base from the Web while controlling the noise of automatic extraction. The objective is to populate a fixed-schema, language-independent repository of disambiguated RDF triples and attach a calibrated probability of correctness to every candidate fact by combining Web extraction evidence with graph-derived Freebase priors.
methodology: Execution pipeline: (1) collect Web free text, HTML DOM trees, HTML tables, and schema.org-annotated pages; (2) for text, run named-entity recognition, POS tagging, dependency parsing, within-document coreference, and entity linking, then train per-predicate distant-supervision logistic-regression extractors from surface/dependency patterns; (3) for DOM pages, learn classifiers from lexicalized DOM paths between linked entities; (4) for tables, link entities and match each unambiguous column to a Freebase predicate; (5) map a subset of schema.org annotations manually to Freebase predicates; (6) merge/de-duplicate source evidence at domain level and fuse the four extractor outputs with per-predicate boosted decision stumps; (7) learn graph priors from Freebase with PRA random-walk path features and a 60-dimensional embedding/MLP link-prediction model, then fuse the priors; (8) fuse extraction and prior scores and calibrate output probabilities with Platt scaling. Labels for supervised training and most testing use the local closed-world assumption (LCWA).

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: The system uses a fixed ontology: entity types and predicates are fixed, and outputs use Freebase entity identifiers and predicates. Freebase supplies both schema and prior facts. HTML-table columns are matched to Freebase predicates; schema.org annotations are manually mapped to 14 mostly person-related Freebase predicates. This constrains extraction but leaves Web entities and relations absent from Freebase unsupported in the current system.

title: Identifying Relations for Open Information Extraction
domain: Unstructured English Web sentences; the relation dictionary is induced from a corpus of 500 million Web sentences, and evaluation uses Web sentences with additional training examples from Wikipedia.
research_problem: The paper addresses incoherent relation phrases and uninformative extractions produced by open-domain relation extractors such as TextRunner and WOE. Its objective is to design simple, scalable constraints that produce more coherent and informative binary verbal relations while retaining broad Web-scale coverage.
methodology: ReVerb operates on POS-tagged and noun-phrase-chunked sentences. For each verb, it identifies the longest contiguous relation phrase matching a verb-centered POS regular expression and passing a lexical frequency constraint. It merges adjacent or overlapping matches, then selects the nearest valid noun phrase to the left and right as arguments. A logistic regression classifier assigns extraction confidence. The lexical dictionary is built offline from 500 million Web sentences; relation phrases are normalized and retained when they take at least 20 distinct argument pairs, yielding approximately 1.7 million normalized phrases.

entity_extraction: ["entity and concept extraction"]
ontology_schema_use: No fixed ontology or relation vocabulary is required. ReVerb uses a corpus-derived dictionary of relation phrases and syntactic/lexical constraints over binary verbal relations; the resulting relations remain open-domain surface phrases.

title: FEEL: Framework for the integration of Entity Extraction and Linking systems
domain: Unstructured plain text in English, including tweets, web pages, news articles, sentences, and mixed-domain documents.
research_problem: The paper addresses the lack of clear guidance for selecting, configuring, invoking, and integrating multiple entity extraction and linking systems. Individual systems differ in domain, language, knowledge-base coverage, parameters, and output formats; combining them can create duplicate or partially overlapping entity tuples. The objective is to provide a reusable ensemble framework and demonstrate it with FEELink.
methodology: FEEL is an ensemble integration framework organized as a sequential pipeline. Parameter Configuration selects EEL services, manages resources, and tunes parameters, especially confidence thresholds. System Invocation prepares requests, handles runtime failures, and parses returned fields. Data Consolidation filters low-frequency, duplicate, and overlapping entity tuples using frequency thresholds, majority voting or ranking, and longest-mention replacement, then prepares RDF Turtle/NIF output. FEELink is the proof-of-concept implementation integrating TagMe, DBpedia Spotlight, Babelfy, and WAT through REST APIs.

ontology_schema_use: The framework links mentions to knowledge-base resources, primarily DBpedia resources, and uses RDF Turtle for final output with the NIF vocabulary for GERBIL annotations. It does not propose a new ontology; schema use is for interoperability and evaluation output.

title: On Aligning OpenIE Extractions with Knowledge Bases: A Case Study
domain: Linked OpenIE triples (subject, surface relation, object) from English Wikipedia, their provenance sentences, and DBpedia facts, relation metadata, entity types, and schema vocabulary.
research_problem: The study examines the limits of aligning ambiguous, surface-relation OpenIE triples to semantically precise DBpedia facts and schemas. It tests the distant-supervision assumption for triples sharing an argument pair with a KB fact, and the implicit one-triple assumption that any OIE triple can be expressed by one KB fact.
methodology: Execution order: (1) start with OPIEC-Linked triples extracted by MinIE-SpaTe from English Wikipedia and retain linked, filtered, correctly extracted triples; (2) use DBpedia ontology facts with disambiguated entity arguments; (3) for the DSA study, find all DBpedia facts sharing an OPIEC triple's entity pair, present facts, types, and relation semantics to an annotator, label each hit as Same/OIE-More-Specific/KB-More-Specific/Different, and retain the best hit; (4) for the OTA study, generate candidates from KB-hit relation counts and then any domain/range-compatible DBpedia relation, label each triple Fully-/Partly-/Not-Expressible with one fact, and manually formulate multi-fact first-order formulas where they improve expressibility; (5) compare information presence in DBpedia; (6) rerun Stanford OIE, OpenIE 5, and RnnOIE on the sampled provenance sentences to assess transferability.
pipeline_stages: ["Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Ontology or schema discovery", "Graph construction", "Knowledge fusion and deduplication", "Graph validation and correction"]

ontology_schema_use: DBpedia is both the reference KB and schema vocabulary. Candidate relations are constrained using DBpedia argument types and relation domain/range information; mapping-based DBpedia ontology triples are retained. The study also tests representation by conjunctive, existential, temporal, and disjunctive KB formulas rather than one fact.

title: MWO2KG and Echidna: Constructing and exploring knowledge graphs from maintenance data
domain: Short, unstructured technical maintenance work-order text combined with structured work-order fields, functional locations, and optionally downtime-event data.
research_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty of extracting useful engineering knowledge from terse, jargon-rich maintenance work-order text and combining it with structured asset records so that reliability engineers can query historical maintenance information, identify failure modes, validate maintenance strategies, and support process improvement.
methodology: MWO2KG converts technical short maintenance text and associated structured fields into a Neo4j knowledge graph. Deployment begins with annotation or import of work orders in Redcoat using maintenance-specific entity types such as item, activity, observation, and location. The annotations are preprocessed to retain at most one entity label per token. A Flair NER model uses pretrained character-level embeddings, a bidirectional LSTM, and a softmax classifier trained with stochastic gradient descent to label entities. A separate Flair text-classification model maps extracted observations to failure-mode codes. Postprocessing adds asset-hierarchy labels using ISO 15926 rules and normalises misspellings and inconsistent names using a manually curated correction dictionary. Triple generation links each item to every other entity in the same short work order through heuristically assigned relations; functional locations are linked to entities in the corresponding work order, and optional downtime events are linked to functional locations with cost and duration properties. The resulting triples are imported into Neo4j. Echidna then visualises and queries the graph, supporting node filtering, aggregation, functional-location filtering, structured-field queries, and failure-mode grouping using ISO 14224 categories. The paper explicitly notes that a relation-extraction step is shown in the generalised architecture but is not implemented in MWO2KG.

ISO 15926 supplies the asset hierarchy used to add parent asset-class labels during postprocessing. ISO 14224 supplies failure-mode categories, condensed to 19 codes for the failure-mode classifier in the described system; the evaluation dataset is also described as originating from 22 ISO 14224 codes. Echidna supports aggregation of classes and subclasses in these hierarchies.

title: Doc‐KG: Unstructured documents to knowledge graph construction, identification and validation with Wikidata
domain: Unstructured natural-language text, including raw document sentences; evaluation inputs are sentences derived from WebNLG's 1-Triple-to-Text corpus and Wikipedia sentences for TinyButMighty.
research_problem: The paper addresses automatic construction and enrichment of knowledge graphs from unstructured natural-language documents, focusing on extracting subject-predicate-object triples and identifying or mapping those triples in Wikidata. It motivates the work by noting the lack of a standard benchmark for triple extraction from unstructured text and the limited prior work on mapping extracted triples to Wikidata.
methodology: Doc-KG is a sequential classical-NLP pipeline. It tokenizes, sentence-splits, lemmatizes, POS-tags, and syntactically parses input text. Dependency labels identify subject and object tokens, while ROOT, AMOD, ADJ, AGENT, and ATTR labels identify predicate tokens. The resulting subject-predicate-object triples are appended to a schema-free local KG. Entity mentions are mapped to Wikidata through exact-label SPARQL queries, with predefined Wikidata URIs for typed values such as dates, numbers, percentages, and money. Predicates are mapped using a locally indexed list of Wikidata properties and alternative labels, followed by stop-word cleaning. The system is compared with SpaCy/Textacy SVO and Stanford CoreNLP OpenIE.

title: Information Extraction meets the Semantic Web: A Survey
domain: Primarily unstructured natural-language text; additionally semi-structured markup documents and web tables.
research_problem: The paper addresses the semantic gap between abundant unstructured Web information and comparatively limited structured Semantic Web content. Its objective is to consolidate literature at the intersection of Information Extraction and Semantic Web technologies, including methods that extract and/or link entities, concepts, and relations from unstructured or semi-structured sources.
methodology: This is a literature survey rather than a newly proposed extraction system. Its review workflow: define section-specific IE and Semantic-Web keyword lists; search their conjunctions in Google Scholar; filter initial results by title/publication type, then abstract, then full paper; extend the seed set through references, citing papers, prominent authors, and newly discovered keywords. The synthesis is organized by entity extraction/linking, concept extraction/linking, relation extraction/linking, semi-structured extraction, and discussion. Within the surveyed relation-extraction literature, the illustrative execution order is entity extraction/linking, relation parsing, property selection/mapping, RDF representation, and evaluation, while explicitly noting that systems need not follow every step or that order.

ontology_schema_use: Semantic Web resources are central to the survey scope. Included work must make non-trivial use of RDF, RDFS, OWL, SKOS, SPARQL, or a resource founded on those standards. Ontologies and knowledge bases can guide extraction and be populated by the extracted results; the survey repeatedly uses DBpedia, Freebase, YAGO, Wikipedia-derived resources, WordNet, and domain ontologies as examples.

title: KBPearl
domain: An incomplete knowledge base plus unstructured natural-language documents; the extraction component receives each document and an OpenIE tool produces open triples.
research_problem: Populate incomplete knowledge bases from unstructured natural-language documents without requiring a predefined set of predicates, while reducing OpenIE redundancy and ambiguity and jointly linking entity and relation phrases to the target KB. The paper specifically targets global coherence in long-text documents and the discovery of entities not already present in the KB.
methodology: KBPearl executes a two-stage text-to-KB population workflow. Stage 1 extracts side information and OpenIE triples, filters noisy triples, resolves basic noun-phrase and relation-phrase variation, and produces canonicalized triples. Stage 2 builds a weighted undirected semantic graph containing noun-phrase, relation-phrase, candidate-entity, and candidate-predicate nodes. Edge weights encode popularity, alias and pattern overlap, and keyphrase-based entity/predicate relatedness. A greedy graph-densification algorithm selects one entity for each noun phrase and one predicate for each relation phrase while maximizing the minimum weighted degree. The system has pipeline and near-neighbour variants; non-linkable noun phrases can be reported as new entities.

title: Exploiting lexical patterns for knowledge graph construction from unstructured text in Spanish
methodology_family: Pattern-based knowledge extraction (lexical/grammatical pattern matching for entity and relation extraction)
domain: Unstructured plain text written in Spanish (UTF-8)
research_problem: Building knowledge graphs from unstructured text in Spanish is challenging because existing structures, models, and strategies designed for other languages (mainly English) are not compatible with Spanish, and no complete solution had been developed to construct KGs from unstructured Spanish text, requiring extraction of named entities and relations, their linking to KG resources, and representation as RDF triples.
methodology: The proposed method is composed of four main stages: (1) text preprocessing, (2) knowledge extraction of named entities and semantic relations via lexical patterns and an NER parser combined with pattern matching, (3) component linking to DBpedia resources with semantic enrichment, and (4) representation, where properties are crafted from predicates and triples are constructed, stored, and visualized.

entity_extraction: ["Knowledge extraction (named entity and semantic relation extraction via lexical patterns)", "Component linking (entity linking and semantic enrichment with DBpedia)"]
relation_extraction: ["Knowledge extraction (named entity and semantic relation extraction via lexical patterns)"]
ontology_schema_use: The method uses DBpedia, RDFS, and OWL vocabularies for existing properties (rdf:type, dcterms:subject, rdf:seeAlso, rdfs:label, owl:sameAs), and additionally defines a custom scheme by crafting new OWL properties (owl:ObjectProperty or owl:DatatypeProperty, with rdfs:domain and rdfs:range) from extracted predicates when no existing ontology property is suitable.

title: ICDM 2019 Knowledge Graph Contest: Team UWA
domain: Unstructured English document text, including domain-specific automotive-engineering and public-security text.
research_problem: Construct a refined, high-quality set of subject–predicate–object triples from domain-specific unstructured documents for the ICDM contest, while avoiding missed domain entities, overly long OpenIE arguments, and fixed relation inventories that do not fit the task.

For visualization, append centrality, NER types, and an LSTM-derived SemEval relation type.

title: Automating Biomedical Knowledge Graph Construction For Context-Aware Scientific Inference
domain: Unstructured biomedical research literature, including PubMed articles, abstracts, introductions, and full-text articles.
research_problem: The paper addresses semantic loss and contradictory evidence caused by representing biomedical interactions as flat, context-agnostic subject-predicate-object triples. It aims to automate extraction, normalization, knowledge fusion, and graph construction from unstructured biomedical literature while preserving entity attributes and the conditions under which relationships hold.
methodology: AutoBioKG uses a LLaMA3.1-8B decoder-only Transformer adapted with LoRA. It generates composite triples of the form (Subject:[Attribute], Relation:[Condition], Object:[Attribute]). A seed model is supervised-fine-tuned on BioOpenIE, then refined once using pseudo-labels from unlabeled PubMed introductions filtered jointly by token confidence and entropy. Extracted entities are normalized to UMLS concepts using candidate retrieval and SapBERT disambiguation; relations are aligned to a dynamic vocabulary using BGE-m3 similarity or added as new relation types. Verified triples are stored in Neo4j, and AutoBioKGAgent exposes extraction, normalization, graph construction, and querying through a natural-language/MCP interface.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and linking"]
relation_extraction: ["Composite relation and triple extraction", "Cross-sentence triplet completion", "Triplet verification and correction", "Relation alignment and schema expansion"]
ontology_schema_use: The core representation is a schema-guided composite triple with optional subject attributes, relation conditions, and object attributes. Entity recognition is constrained by 23 UMLS semantic types; entity normalization uses UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers; the initial relation vocabulary is derived from the UMLS Semantic Network and can expand dynamically.

title: Enhancing Domain-Independent Knowledge Graph Construction through OpenIE Cleaning and LLMs Validation
domain: Raw unstructured natural-language text, including computer-science article abstracts and a music document
research_problem: The paper addresses automatic construction of knowledge graphs from raw, unstructured text when domain-specific NER and relation-extraction systems improve precision but reduce domain independence, while OpenIE preserves broad coverage but produces many incorrect triplets. The objective is to build a reusable, domain-independent pipeline that cleans OpenIE outputs and validates extracted triplets against their source sentences using an LLM.
methodology: G-T2KG processes raw text through five sequential components. C1 performs corpus cleaning, coreference resolution, and sentence segmentation. C2 extracts triplets with OpenIE6 and extracts hypernym or is-a relations with a pattern-based Hypernym Relation Extractor. C3 cleans OpenIE triplets using predicate rectification, stopword removal, lemmatization, noun-phrase checks, and either Stanford CoreNLP dependency-tree analysis (Option 1) or zero-shot GPT-4 head identification (Option 2). Cleaned OpenIE triplets are merged with hypernym triplets. C4 validates each triplet by converting it into an affirmation and asking GPT-4 whether it corresponds to the source sentence; invalid triplets are filtered. C5 maps entities and predicates using the approach adopted from SciCero to reduce label heterogeneity. Mapping is deliberately performed after validation so that mapped labels not present in the sentence do not complicate verification. The architecture is therefore a modular hybrid of symbolic/syntactic processing, neural OpenIE, pattern-based extraction, zero-shot LLM cleaning/validation, and post-extraction mapping. The paper does not report entity typing as part of the implemented pipeline.

The evaluation uses manually constructed gold standards rather than an ontology-driven target schema.

title: Entity Linking: An Issue to Extract Corresponding Entity With Knowledge Base
domain: Unstructured web text, including news articles, short texts, tweets, and query text containing named entities.
research_problem: The paper surveys entity linking as the problem of identifying ambiguous named-entity mentions in natural-language text and mapping them to the corresponding entities in a knowledge base, including deciding when a mention has no corresponding knowledge-base entity. It positions entity linking as a prerequisite for knowledge-base population and knowledge fusion.
methodology: This is a survey and framework paper rather than a single newly trained entity-linking system. Its general execution pipeline is: (1) detect query mentions with named-entity recognition or word segmentation; (2) generate candidate entities from a knowledge base using a surface-form dictionary, direct indexed search, or mention-entity probability p(e|m); (3) rank or classify candidates using context similarity, lexical/type/popularity/topic features, probabilistic or classical machine-learning models, neural semantic representations, or graph-based collective inference; (4) select the top entity when its score exceeds a threshold, otherwise output NIL; and (5) optionally cluster NIL mentions referring to the same unseen entity using string similarity, hierarchical agglomerative clustering, or semantic graphs. The paper also distinguishes coreference resolution, which clusters mentions within text, from entity linking, which maps mentions to knowledge-base entities.

title: Incorporating Contexts to Open Information Extraction
domain: English unstructured open-domain natural-language text: source sentences, optionally surrounding document sentences; SpecTup additionally receives an extracted relational tuple aligned to its source sentence.
research_problem: Improve the accuracy, contextual interpretation, efficiency, and reliability of open-domain relational-tuple extraction. The thesis identifies flexible open-form tuple representations, difficult evaluation, insufficient gold training data, sentence-only extraction, underused syntax, token-level span granularity, and speculative/non-factual tuples as central problems. It treats OpenIE tuples as candidate structured facts usable for KB/KG construction, but does not itself implement a complete knowledge-graph construction system.
methodology: The thesis contributes four complementary context-aware OpenIE methods. (1) DocIE: for each source sentence, concatenate neighbouring document sentences with segment embeddings; BERT bottom blocks model source-context interactions, top Transformer blocks retain source-token representations, and a CopyAttention-style LSTM decoder with attention/copying generates relational tuples. (2) SMiLe-OIE: convert dependency trees and flattened constituency trees into word-node graphs; encode BERT token representations plus relation indicators using dependency and constituency GCNs; fuse the two views using auxiliary intra-view and inter-view multi-view losses; predict BIO-style argument/relation tags for n-ary tuples. (3) Chunk-OIE: represent a sentence as a sequence of chunks (SaC), encode chunk type and chunk-level dependency structure with BERT and a dependency GCN, and learn chunking and OpenIE extraction in either two stages or end-to-end multi-task training. (4) SpecTup/OIE-Spec: after tuples are extracted, mark tuple relation tokens, encode sentence semantics with BERT, aggregate one-hop dependency neighbours of the relation using a relation-aware GCN, concatenate semantic and syntactic representations, and classify each tuple as speculative/non-speculative (optionally one of six modal classes). No entity linking, coreference resolution, canonicalization, graph fusion, or graph materialization is performed by these proposed systems.

ontology_schema_use: Open-schema extraction: OpenIE is explicitly not restricted to predefined relation/entity types or an ontology. Outputs are open-form binary or n-ary tuples. Existing KB schemas are discussed only as downstream mappings from OpenIE tuples, not as constraints used by the proposed models.
