title: Generative Knowledge Graph Construction: A Review
domain: Unstructured natural-language text, including sentences and documents; certain reviewed methods additionally take a schema, task specification, or event template as input.
research_problem: A survey problem: generative KGC methods had become distributed across entity recognition, relation extraction, event extraction, entity linking, and KG completion, without a systematic review or common comparison. The paper organizes and analyzes these methods, which use Seq2Seq generation to extract or generate KG-relevant structures from text and thereby avoid the task-specific pipeline limitations of error propagation and poor cross-task adaptability.
methodology: The paper surveys generative KGC as conditional sequence generation: unstructured text x is mapped to a linearized structural target y, then inverse-linearized or decoded into entities, relations/triples, event structures, links, or KG-completion outputs. It proposes five generation-target paradigms in execution terms: (1) copy-based sequences copy entity tokens while generating relation tokens from a restricted vocabulary; (2) structure-linearized sequences serialize a target graph/event/triple structure, often with schema-constrained decoding; (3) label-augmented sequences reproduce input text with bracketed natural-language labels; (4) indice-based sequences generate begin/end and label indices via pointer-style decoding; and (5) blank-based sequences fill role placeholders in event templates. The review compares semantic utilization, decoding search space, application scope, and template cost; theoretically analyzes output-space/semantic trade-offs and decoding; and aggregates reported NYT and ACE-2005 results from prior work. Contributions explicitly stated by the authors are a detailed taxonomy, theoretical and empirical analysis, and future directions.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Schema use is central to several reviewed generative approaches. Targets may be restricted to a predefined schema; structural/event schemas constrain decoding and validate semantic/structural legitimacy. The review describes prefix-tree decoding based on predefined schemas and label-semantic or template-based representations. It does not propose a new ontology or schema itself.

title: Knowledge-Based Weak Supervision for Information Extraction of Overlapping Relations
domain: Unstructured New York Times news-text sentences, preprocessed into sentences containing two phrases matched to Freebase entities; training additionally uses Freebase binary facts and relation names.
research_problem: Learn relation extractors from a structured database and unstructured text without manually labelled sentences, while overcoming noisy heuristic database-text matches and the incorrect assumption that one entity pair can have only one relation. The target is binary relation extraction from New York Times sentences, including overlapping Freebase relations for the same entity pair.
methodology: MULTIR groups all sentences containing an entity pair. For every candidate relation it creates a Boolean corpus-level fact variable Y^r, so multiple relations may simultaneously be true; each sentence has a latent label Z_i in the relation set plus none. Relation-sensitive lexical, POS, named-entity, and dependency-path features score sentence labels. Deterministic OR join factors require every positive aggregate fact to be expressed by at least one sentence. Weak labels are relation bit-vectors obtained from Freebase facts for matched entity pairs. Training uses online, Viterbi-approximated hidden-variable perceptron updates: compare an unconstrained best assignment with the best latent sentence assignment consistent with database labels and update their feature difference. At prediction, unconstrained sentence labels are independently selected and induce aggregate facts; label-constrained training inference is reduced to weighted edge cover and greedily approximated in O(|R|·|S|). This is relation extraction rather than joint entity-and-relation extraction: entity mentions and their matching to Freebase are preprocessing inputs.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Freebase supplies the closed inventory of relation names R and atomic binary facts Δ used as weak aggregate labels. Its entity names are also used to match detected text phrases. The paper does not perform ontology discovery; Freebase is an external schema/knowledge-base constraint for supervision and output relation labels.

title: Learning to Link with Wikipedia
domain: Plain, unstructured natural-language documents; evaluated on Wikipedia article text with markup removed and on English newswire stories.
research_problem: Automatically wikify unstructured text: detect the terms/topics that merit links and disambiguate each to the intended Wikipedia article. The objective is to add explanatory cross-references and thereby transform plain text into an unambiguous, structured set or graph of Wikipedia concepts.
methodology: Execution pipeline: (1) obtain candidate n-grams from a document and retain those above a low Wikipedia link-probability threshold; (2) disambiguate candidate anchors to Wikipedia articles using a C4.5 classifier over sense commonness, weighted semantic relatedness to unambiguous context articles, and context quality; (3) merge phrase-to-article associations into candidate topics; (4) apply a bagged C4.5 link-detector classifier to select link-worthy topics using average/max link probability, relatedness, disambiguation confidence, category-tree generality, and mention frequency, first/last occurrence, and spread; (5) create links to selected Wikipedia topics. For illustrative graph construction, extracted topics are connected when their Wikipedia link-based relatedness is significant.
pipeline_stages: ["Text preprocessing", "Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking", "Graph construction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: Wikipedia is the controlled target vocabulary/knowledge base: candidate phrases are resolved to Wikipedia articles. Wikipedia anchor statistics supply priors and labels; incoming/outgoing link structure supplies semantic relatedness; its category hierarchy supplies a generality feature. The paper illustrates optional connection to DBpedia/YAGO for more formal reasoning, but does not use an externally specified ontology as a mandatory extraction schema.

title: LINDEN: Linking Named Entities with Knowledge Base via Semantic Knowledge
domain: An unstructured textual document with named-entity mentions already detected; Wikipedia text is also supported through its wiki markup.
research_problem: Entity linking for knowledge-base population: map each already-recognized named-entity mention in unstructured text to its corresponding real-world entity in a knowledge base, or return NIL when no corresponding entity exists. The method specifically targets name ambiguity, name variation/textual inconsistency, and the inability of bag-of-words context overlap to capture semantic relations.
methodology: Execution pipeline: (1) take one document containing named-entity mentions detected beforehand; (2) construct/look up a Wikipedia-derived surface-form dictionary built from entity pages, redirects, disambiguation pages, and article hyperlinks, retaining target counts and pruning very-low-link-probability candidates; (3) recognize Wikipedia context concepts, using Wikipedia-Miner for general text or wiki markup for Wikipedia text; (4) construct a semantic network over context concepts and candidates using Wikipedia link relations/articles plus YAGO taxonomic relations; (5) compute link probability (LP), Wikipedia-link-based semantic associativity (SA), taxonomy-based semantic similarity (SS), and document-level global coherence (GC); (6) rank candidates with a learned linear max-margin/SVM weight vector; and (7) return the highest-scoring candidate only when it passes a learned threshold, otherwise NIL. GC approximates collective assignment by using the highest-LP candidate for each other mention.

entity_extraction: ["Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: YAGO is the target knowledge base and supplies a clean WordNet-derived taxonomy. LINDEN adds taxonomic relations between context concepts and candidate entities to its semantic network and derives semantic similarity from their sets of superclasses. This is an ontology used for candidate disambiguation and linking, not ontology/schema discovery.

title: Llm-Tikg: Threat Intelligence Knowledge Graph Construction Utilizing Large Language Model
domain: Unstructured English open-source cyber-threat-intelligence reports, including security-company content, security news, and personal security blogs; reports may contain prose, IoC lists, and tables.
research_problem: The paper addresses automated construction of a threat-intelligence knowledge graph from unstructured open-source cyber-threat reports. It targets fragmented IoC extraction, domain-specific and ambiguous entity recognition, limited handling of long reports, expensive manual annotation, and the omission of attack-behavior descriptions and MITRE ATT&CK TTP information needed for attack-chain analysis, intrusion detection, and attribution.
methodology: LLM-TIKG is a multi-stage pipeline. First, web crawlers collect report title, link, and cleaned content from security-company platforms, security news, and personal security blogs. GPT-3.5-turbo is prompted with task instructions, demonstrations, and report text to generate labels for topic classification, entity/relation extraction, and TTP classification. For entity/relation data, prompts specify entity types and output examples; filtering rules remove unsupported entity types, keep only relations whose endpoints are extracted entities, and manually correct part of the generated labels. TTP data combines MITRE ATT&CK malware-behavior examples with Tram data and is augmented by back-translation and GPT rewriting. Llama2-7B is instruction-tuned with LoRA on instruction/input/output examples. At inference, the model classifies reports using title and first-paragraph content, skips non-threat reports, extracts end-of-report IoCs with regular expressions and connects them to the report's main object, processes reports section by section, extracts entities and relations, and classifies TTPs sentence by sentence for reports centered on malware or attackers. Post-processing resolves generic references to preceding entities, attaches the report's main object to reduce cross-instance ambiguity, merges malware aliases with rules, clusters attack types and relationships using embeddings, cosine distance, and hierarchical agglomerative clustering, and stores the resulting graph in Neo4j.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and alias fusion"]
ontology_schema_use: The method uses a task-defined schema with entity categories Malware, Threat Type, Attacker, Technique, Tool, Vulnerability, IP, Domain, URL, File, and Hash, plus prompted relationship tuples. TTP classification is grounded in the MITRE ATT&CK technique and sub-technique taxonomy; the experiment reports 229 technique categories and 595 sub-technique categories represented in the dataset. The paper does not describe a separate formal KG ontology.

title: LLM4Schema.org: Generating Schema.org Markups With Large Language Models
domain: Rendered webpage HTML and its visible body text, together with a selected Schema.org target type; the evaluation also uses existing human-authored JSON-LD markup from the webpage.
research_problem: The paper addresses how to generate reliable and sufficiently complete Schema.org JSON-LD markups from real, potentially lengthy webpage text when no complete ground-truth markup exists. It specifically investigates whether LLM-generated markup can outperform human-generated markup after filtering syntactic invalidity, unsupported statements, and violations of Schema.org property expectations.
methodology: LLM4Schema.org first extracts webpage body text and selects a target Schema.org type. An LLM is prompted with the target type, its allowed properties, Schema.org documentation examples, and the webpage content to generate JSON-LD. Long text is split into overlapping chunks and the outputs are merged. A custom SHACL-based Validity agent removes syntactically invalid types, properties, and values. An LLM-based Factuality agent checks each property-value-type triple against the webpage text, while an LLM-based Compliance agent checks each property value against the Schema.org property definition. The curated human and LLM markups are compared using the MIMR metric.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction"]
ontology_schema_use: Uses the Schema.org ontology as the target schema, including its types, properties, inheritance relationships, expected value types, and natural-language property definitions. The paper reports 806 types and 1476 properties. Generated JSON-LD is constrained and validated against Schema.org-derived SHACL shapes; compliance is checked against Schema.org documentation.

title: LLMs for Knowledge Graph Construction and Reasoning: Recent Capabilities and Future Opportunities
domain: Natural-language sentences for relation/triple extraction and event detection; KG triples with a masked tail entity for link prediction; natural-language questions for KBQA; synthetic/Re-TACRED-derived sentences with invented entity and relation names for VINE; and a user task/dialogue plus optional internet/external-source information for AutoKG.
research_problem: The study asks how capable general-purpose LLMs are, without task-specific training, at representative KG construction and reasoning tasks; whether apparent information-extraction success reflects memorized pre-training knowledge or contextual generalization; and how LLMs plus external information and communicative agents could support automatic KG construction and reasoning.
methodology: The work has three connected components. (1) It prompts text-davinci-003, ChatGPT, and GPT-4 in zero- and one-shot settings for relation/triple extraction, event detection, link prediction, and KBQA, comparing their scores with fully supervised task baselines. Prompts constrain the allowed relations/event labels where appropriate and request structured triple or label answers. (2) It creates VINE from Re-TACRED by replacing real entities and relations with invented ones, then asks models to extract virtual SPO triples after relation-specific demonstrations, to probe generalization beyond memorized facts. (3) It proposes AutoKG: a role-playing multi-agent concept using a task specifier, KG-domain-expert user, consultant/KG assistant, and web-searcher; agents iteratively clarify the task, retrieve external information when indicated, and produce a KG. The paper shows one qualitative movie-KG example rather than a controlled AutoKG benchmark.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction"]
ontology_schema_use: Task-provided schemas constrain several prompted evaluations: SciERC and DuIE2.0 provide allowed predicate lists, and event detection provides an event-type list. AutoKG may use external knowledge bases or existing KGs, but the paper does not specify an ontology language, a schema-discovery algorithm, or formal graph constraints.

title: Open Relation Extraction and Grounding
domain: English open-domain natural-language documents and sentences, processed with linguistic annotations; the evaluation corpus contains news documents, web blogs, and discussion-forum posts.
research_problem: Open relation extraction between entities in open-domain text: extract salient relational triples rather than many syntactically possible but unimportant pairs, and assign each retained pair a meaningful KB relation type (or NONE) when surface relation phrases are diverse, implicit, or overly specific.
methodology: For each sentence, the system parses uncollapsed dependencies, adds lower-weight reverse edges, annotates entity/time types, and resolves coreference to create an extended dependency graph. Every entity pair is a candidate. It computes directed random-walk first-passage and symmetric commute-time distances, then an entity-preferred TextRank-like importance score. Relation strength is entity-importance product divided by squared commute distance; a maximum spanning tree keeps salient pairs and first-passage asymmetry orders their arguments. For each retained pair, nouns, verbs, adjectives, prepositions, and particles receive commute-time-based context weights. Grounding compares an argument-difference/context-word embedding with KB-relation embeddings built from DBpedia triple translations and relation-name embeddings; type constraints filter incompatible KB relations, and the best remaining relation is selected or marked NONE.

entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Entity resolution and linking"]
ontology_schema_use: DBpedia supplies the target relation schema, relation triples, relation names, and argument-type constraints. Candidate triples are grounded to a DBpedia relation or NONE; for Slot Filling evaluation, DBpedia relations are manually mapped to TAC-KBP slot types, with location subtypes assigned by gazetteer matching.

title: Question-Answer Extraction from Scientific Articles Using Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models
domain: Full-text scientific articles with title, abstract, keywords, XML paragraphs, and article chunks used for triplet extraction.
research_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty researchers face when identifying and understanding the main ideas, contributions, and novelty of large numbers of scientific articles. It aims to generate concise, targeted QA pairs from full-text articles, with the KG-based method additionally representing article content in the context of the broader literature so that questions can focus on salient and potentially novel information.
methodology: The paper presents two sequential QA-generation pipelines. CCQG parses XML articles into paragraphs, represents the title, abstract, and keywords as a proxy, selects paragraphs whose sentence-transformer similarity exceeds a threshold, prompts GPT-3.5 to generate questions, ranks and filters questions, generates answers from associated paragraphs, and removes answers flagged by SelfCheckGPT. The KG-based pipeline selects representative seed documents using TopicBert topic clusters and KMeans, prompts an LLM to extract entity-relation triplets from article chunks, fine-tunes domain-specific REBEL models, builds a per-article KG in Neo4j, computes triplet saliency from entity/triplet TF-IDF, PageRank, graph structure, and semantic similarity to metadata, then prompts GPT-3.5 with salient triplets and paragraphs to generate and rank questions and answers.

title: Relation-Faceted Graph Pooling with LLM Guidance for Dynamic Span-Aware Information Extraction
domain: Unstructured natural-language text, evaluated as sentences from newswire, scientific abstracts, and ACE05's diverse text domains.
research_problem: Joint information extraction from unstructured text: extract semantically valid (head span, relation, tail span) triples while classifying entity types. The work targets two stated limitations of existing span-/token-pair approaches: static spans formed without relational context and relation-agnostic validation that does not provide a clear basis for LLM semantic grounding.
methodology: RePooL is a relation-faceted text-to-graph framework with five depicted modules. It constructs a dual-view token/relation graph using subject_of, object_of, and compound_with structural relations; scores and top-K filters tokens; composes and filters candidate token-level triples using [HEAD]/[REL]/[TAIL]/[CLS] representations; updates nodes through validity-weighted aggregation; composes contiguous validated tokens into pooled multi-token spans; then performs analogous span-level triple validation. An LLM compares candidate triple sets, and its preferences are transferred through BPR pairwise alignment. At prediction, candidate triples are ranked by validity score and top-ranked triples are output; training combines prefiltering, alignment, and prediction objectives.
pipeline_stages: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing", "Relation and triple extraction", "Graph construction", "Graph validation and correction"]
entity_extraction: ["Entity and concept extraction", "Entity typing"]
ontology_schema_use: The method uses a fixed task relation inventory as relation nodes and introduces three auxiliary structural relation labels (subject_of, object_of, compound_with) for graph construction and span composition. The presentation does not report use of an external ontology or ontology-discovery procedure.
